contentBlocks.text: This week's skills solve a genuinely common real-world problem: figuring out a total cost that has both a flat fee and a per-unit rate.

A taxi charges a $3 base fee plus $2 per mile. This is a linear relationship: y = 2x + 3, where x is miles and y is total cost — $3 is the y-intercept (the base fee you pay even for 0 miles), and $2 is the slope (the rate per mile). For 5 miles: y = 2(5) + 3 = $13. Find the total cost for an 8-mile ride using this same equation.
You just used a linear equation to solve a real cost problem. Tomorrow we'll review everything about linear equations and functions from this whole week.

objectives: Set up a linear equation (y=mx+b) from a real-world flat-fee-plus-rate scenario
Solve for a total cost using the equation
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's slope and slope-intercept skills.
2. Work through the taxi example together, identifying the base fee (b) and rate (m).
3. Have the child solve the 8-mile version independently.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: explicitly label 'base fee = b' and 'rate per unit = m' before writing the equation each time
Ready for more: ask them to write and solve their own flat-fee-plus-rate scenario (a phone plan, a gym membership)
This is exactly how real subscription/rate pricing works — worth connecting to something the child has actually seen (a data plan, a rideshare app)
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. y=2x+3 at x=5 gives y=$13. 2. y=2x+3 at x=8 gives y=$19. 3. The base fee is the y-intercept ($3); the per-mile rate is the slope ($2).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 8 Expressions & Equations standard 8.EE.8/Functions 8.F.4: constructing and using a linear function to model a real-world relationship between two quantities.
